name: 苦盐田
The Bitter Salt Pans
before: 南边沙漠里一片白，白得晃眼，是一大片盐田。几十个戴脚镣的人弯着腰耙盐，耙一天，换两个馕。看守是国舅府的盐监，带着弓手、铁骑和戟士，一人一根浸了盐水的鞭子。耙盐的人里有个十八九岁的后生，脚镣比别人粗一圈，盐监说他是「贼，还是贼的儿子」。

In the southern desert lies a blinding whiteness: a great salt pan. Dozens of men in leg irons bend over raking salt, a day's raking for two naan. The overseers are the Royal Uncle's salt wardens with archers, cavalry and halberdiers, each holding a whip soaked in brine. Among the rakers is a lad of eighteen or nineteen whose irons are a size heavier than the rest. He's 'a thief', the warden says, 'and a thief's son too'.
after: 盐监跑了，脚镣砸开。后生叫葛小轮，他爹葛大轮是千里号的车把式。他找爹找到王城，旧案簿上写着：「葛大轮，盗王城水车一辆，在逃。」他要替爹洗冤，没过一个月，自己也成了贼。他捧起一把盐：「这儿原先是湖，太阳把水一年年晒干，水走了，盐走不了。」

The wardens flee and the irons are smashed. The lad is Ge Xiaolun; his father, Ge Dalun, was the Qianli caravan's carter. He followed his father's trail all the way to the King's city, where the old case register reads: 'Ge Dalun. Stole one royal water cart. At large.' He set out to clear his father's name, and within a month was a thief himself. He scoops up a handful of salt. 'This was a lake once. Year by year the sun dried the water off. The water could leave. The salt couldn't.'

name: 三寸讼棚
Three-Inch Law Booth
before: 路边一个芦席棚，门口挂着块木牌：「代写状纸，包赢，赢了给个瓜。」棚子正被一伙人拆：国舅府的打手，步卒、弓手、骑手都有，来头不小。棚主是个瘦小的讼师，外号麻三寸，舌头三寸，个子也就比舌头高一点。他抱着一摞状纸缩在桌子底下，嘴还没停：「打人犯律！拆棚子另算！」

A reed-mat booth by the road, a board at its door: 'Petitions written. Win guaranteed. Pay one melon if you win.' It's being torn down by the Royal Uncle's thugs, foot, archers and horse together, no small party. The owner is a scrawny advocate nicknamed Three-Inch Ma, for his three-inch tongue; he himself stands not much taller than it. He's huddled under his table clutching a pile of petitions, mouth still going: 'Assault is against the law! The booth is a separate charge!'
after: 打手们跑了，麻三寸从桌子底下爬出来，掸掸灰，听葛小轮讲完，一拍桌子：「这案子我接了，一个瓜。」他扳着指头数：先找那只「偷来」的银碗，再找一个看见的人，最后翻十年前那辆水车的旧账。「三样齐了，」他说，「死案也能说活。」

The thugs gone, Three-Inch Ma crawls out from under the table, dusts himself off, hears Ge Xiaolun out and slaps the table. 'I'll take it. One melon.' He counts on his fingers: first find the 'stolen' silver bowl, then find someone who saw, and last dig out the ten-year-old accounts of that water cart. 'Get all three,' he says, 'and I can talk a dead case back to life.'

name: 沙底当
The Sand Pawnshop
before: 沙窝里挖了个地窖，窖口挂着个「当」字，是走私客开的黑当铺，什么都收，不问来路。一伙骑手在窖口守着，见生人就绕着你转圈子扬沙。葛小轮被判偷的那只银碗，麻三寸打听到就当在这里：碗底刻着一枝葡萄，跟当票上写的一模一样。

A cellar dug into a hollow in the sand with a 'PAWN' sign at its mouth: a smugglers' black pawnshop that takes anything and asks nothing. Riders guard the entrance and circle any stranger, kicking up sand. Three-Inch Ma has learned that the silver bowl Ge Xiaolun was convicted of stealing is pawned here: a vine spray engraved on the bottom, exactly as the ticket describes.
after: 骑手们被打散，当铺掌柜乖乖翻出了底簿。那只银碗当在三个月前，比葛小轮「偷碗」还早了一个月，当碗的人画的押是「府中刘」。麻三寸把底簿那一页撕下来，叠好塞进鞋里：「碗还在宫里就被当了，那他偷的是哪只？」

The riders scattered, the pawnbroker meekly produces his ledger. The bowl was pawned three months before, a full month before Ge Xiaolun supposedly stole it, and the pawner signed 'Liu of the House'. Three-Inch Ma tears out the page, folds it and tucks it in his shoe. 'The bowl was pawned while it was still supposed to be in the palace. So which bowl did he steal?'

name: 捕雀林
Bird-Net Wood
before: 湖南岸的林子里张满了细网，网上挂着扑腾的黄雀。一个干瘦的捕雀老汉被一队国舅府的弓手看着，天天替国舅的花园捕鸟，捕不够数就挨饿。麻三寸说要找的证人就是他：那天集市上，他就蹲在葛小轮旁边卖鸟。老汉一看见你们，赶紧把头埋进鸟笼后头。

In the woods on the lake's south shore fine nets hang everywhere, yellow finches fluttering in them. A gaunt old bird catcher is kept here under guard by the Royal Uncle's archers, netting birds for the Royal Uncle's garden every day and going hungry when he falls short. He's the witness, says Three-Inch Ma: on market day he was squatting right beside Ge Xiaolun selling birds. As soon as he sees you, the old man ducks behind his cages.
after: 弓手们跑了，老汉把笼门一个个打开，黄雀扑棱棱飞了一林子。他这才开口：那天一个穿府里衣裳的人，从背后往葛小轮的包袱里塞了一样亮东西，转身就喊「抓贼」。那人走时还笑了一句：「老的偷车，小的偷碗，一家子贼。」

The archers flee and the old man opens the cages one by one; finches flutter out all through the wood. Only then does he talk. That day a man in the House's livery slipped something shiny into Ge Xiaolun's bundle from behind, then turned and shouted 'Thief!' As he left he laughed: 'The old one steals a cart, the young one steals a bowl. A family of thieves.'

name: 逃营沙
Deserters' Dunes
before: 沙丘间扎着一座破营，营里戟士、弓手、骑手都有，穿的是王城禁军的号衣，可号衣上的徽记都拆了。这是一伙逃兵，见人就躲，躲不过就打。葛小轮认出了领头的：当初押他去盐田的就是这人。领头的也认出了他，脸一红，刀却没放下。

Among the dunes stands a ragged camp of halberdiers, archers and riders in the uniforms of the King's guard, every badge torn off. Deserters: they hide from anyone they see and fight when they can't. Ge Xiaolun recognises their leader as the man who marched him off to the salt pans. The leader recognises him too and reddens, but doesn't lower his blade.
after: 逃兵们服了，领头的跟葛小轮赔了不是。他们逃出来，是因为国舅接管禁军以后，操练改成了给府里扛水缸。他说禁军里只有一个人教过真本事：铁教头。葛小轮的案子以后，铁教头就被赶出了城，听说在南边沙里，还在练兵，「练的是一帮孩子」。

The deserters yield, and their leader apologises to Ge Xiaolun. They ran, he says, because once the Royal Uncle took over the guard, drill became carrying water jars for his house. Only one man in the guard ever taught real skills: Drill Master Tie. After the Ge case he was driven from the city, and they hear he's somewhere in the southern sands, still drilling. 'Drilling a pack of children.'

name: 焚卷车
The Burning Cart
before: 沙路上走着一队车，车上装满了木箱，前后押着戟士、弓手和铁骑，车尾还拖着一桶火油。麻三寸一看箱子上的封条就跳了起来：是王城刑房的旧案卷，国舅府下了令，「十年以上的旧卷，一律焚毁」。千里号那桩水车案，正好十年。

A line of carts rolls along the desert road, loaded with wooden chests and guarded fore and aft by halberdiers, archers and cavalry, a barrel of lamp oil dragging behind. One look at the seals on the chests and Three-Inch Ma jumps: the old case files of the city's court of punishments. The Royal Uncle's house has ordered all files more than ten years old burnt. The Qianli water cart case is exactly ten.
after: 押车的跑了，火油桶滚进了沙沟。麻三寸翻了半天，翻出了那一卷：「葛大轮盗王城水车一辆」。可卷末还夹着城门的出入记：水车是夜里从西门出去的，守门的批了四个字：「持王令出。」麻三寸眯起眼：「拿着王令偷东西的贼，我还是头一回见。」

The escort flees and the oil barrel rolls into a gully. After much rummaging Three-Inch Ma finds the roll: 'Ge Dalun stole one royal water cart.' But tucked at the end is the city gate's log: the cart went out of the west gate at night, and the gatekeeper noted four words: 'Left bearing royal warrant.' Ma narrows his eyes. 'A thief who steals with the King's warrant in his hand. That's a first.'

name: 猎屋林
Hunting Lodge Wood
before: 林子里一座木头猎屋，原来是湖边猎户歇脚的地方，如今被国舅府的一队家丁占了，当成了伏路的哨所，屋里屋外挂满了打来的野鸭和黄羊。猎户老秦被赶到屋后的狗棚里住，他的猎狗倒被家丁拴在门口，替他们看门，看见老秦就摇尾巴，不敢叫。

A log hunting lodge in the woods, once a resting place for the lakeside hunters, now taken by a squad of the Royal Uncle's household men as a roadside watch post, wild ducks and gazelles hanging everywhere inside and out. Old Qin the hunter has been turned out to live in the dog shed behind, while his hound is tied at the door to guard it for them. Whenever it sees Old Qin it wags its tail, too scared to bark.
after: 家丁被赶跑，猎狗挣开绳子扑进了老秦怀里。老秦认得葛小轮：两年前那孩子一路问到这里，问「有没有见过一辆王城的水车」，老秦留他住了三天。「这孩子死心眼，」老秦说，「跟他爹一样。他爹当年也在这屋里住过一宿。」

The household men driven off, the hound breaks its rope and leaps into Old Qin's arms. Old Qin knows Ge Xiaolun: two years ago the boy came asking his way here, 'Have you seen a royal water cart?', and Qin put him up for three days. 'Stubborn boy,' says Old Qin. 'Like his father. His father spent a night in this lodge too, back then.'
first: 猎屋里抄出二十只风干野鸭、四条黄羊腿、一坛酸奶疙瘩、一捆箭，还有家丁们记的「伏路簿」：葛小轮、麻三寸，名字后面都画了圈。

The lodge yields twenty wind-dried wild ducks, four gazelle legs, a crock of dried curd, a bundle of arrows, and the household men's 'ambush register' with circles drawn after the names Ge Xiaolun and Three-Inch Ma.
pass: 每次路过，老秦都从梁上取下一串熏好的野鸭，再让猎狗领你们走一条近道，绕开湖边的烂泥：「狗认路，比人强。」
Every time you pass, Old Qin takes down a string of smoked ducks from the rafters and has his hound lead you by a short cut round the lakeside mud. 'A dog knows the way better than a man.'

name: 围场沙
The Besieged Drill Ground
before: 南边沙里有一片用石头圈出来的场子，场上插着一排木桩，桩上挂着草人。场子外头围着一伙赏金弓手，国舅府出了一百两金子，要铁教头那本禁军操典。他们放箭不往人身上射，专射场上的草人，射一个，场子里就有孩子哭一声。场子中央站着一个独臂老头，一声不吭，手里攥着一根木枪。

In the southern sands lies a ground ringed with stones, a row of stakes hung with straw men. Outside it a band of bounty archers waits: the Royal Uncle's house has offered a hundred taels of gold for Drill Master Tie's manual of the King's guard. They don't shoot at people. They shoot the straw men, and every time one is hit a child inside cries out. In the middle stands a one-armed old man, silent, gripping a wooden spear.
after: 赏金弓手跑了，场子里钻出三十来个孩子，大的十二三，小的才六七岁，个个手里一根木棍。铁教头没道谢，先让孩子们把散了的队列站好，一个个点过数，才转过身来：「明天再来。今天的操，还没练完。」

The bounty archers flee and some thirty children emerge from the ground, the oldest twelve or thirteen, the youngest six or seven, each holding a wooden staff. Drill Master Tie doesn't thank you. First he has the children re-form their broken ranks and counts them one by one; only then does he turn round. 'Come back tomorrow. Today's drill isn't finished.'

name: 守门翁
The Old Gatekeeper
before: 沙地里一间半塌的土屋，住着一个耳朵背的老头，十年前是王城西门的守门人。一伙国舅府的戟士正在拆他的屋顶，说这片地「府里要了」，拆完了还要把他送去盐田。老头坐在门槛上，抱着一只旧灯笼，谁拆都不挪窝：「我在门口坐了三十年，坐惯了。」

A half-collapsed mud hut in the sand, home to a hard-of-hearing old man who was gatekeeper of the city's west gate ten years ago. Some of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers are tearing off his roof, saying 'the House wants this land', and when they're done they mean to send him to the salt pans. He sits on his doorstep hugging an old lantern and won't budge for anyone. 'Thirty years I sat at a gate. I'm used to it.'
after: 戟士们跑了。老头记得那一夜：水车是老王的车，车夫是个黑脸汉子，车上装满了水囊，旁边坐着一个瘦先生，提着盏灯，递给他一块王令。老头问要不要登记，那先生说：「不必，这车我记在账上了。」麻三寸听完，长出一口气：「记在账上的，叫借，不叫偷。」

The halberdiers flee. The old man remembers that night: it was the old King's own cart, the driver a dark-faced man, the cart loaded with waterskins, and beside him a thin gentleman with a lamp, who handed over a royal token. The old man asked whether to log it. 'No need,' the gentleman said. 'I've entered this cart in my accounts.' Three-Inch Ma lets out a long breath. 'What's entered in the accounts is a loan, not a theft.'

name: 沙公堂
The Sand Court
before: 沙地上摆了一张公案，国舅府养的一个判官坐在后头，戟士两排站开，要「缺席再判」：葛小轮私逃盐田，罪加一等。判官看见麻三寸就笑：「你个讨瓜吃的，也配上堂？」又瞅瞅你们的旗子：「哪儿来的叫花子商队，旗子都补了三块。」

A judge's bench has been set up on the sand, a judge kept by the Royal Uncle's house sitting behind it, halberdiers in two rows, ready to 'retry in absence': Ge Xiaolun has escaped the salt pans, so his crime is raised a degree. The judge laughs at the sight of Three-Inch Ma. 'A melon beggar like you, fit to plead in court?' He squints at your banner. 'And what beggars' caravan is this? Three patches on the flag.'
after: 戟士们一倒，判官从公案底下爬出来，跪着把那份判词双手捧给麻三寸，又自己掏钱买了两个瓜，一个给麻三寸，一个塞给你们的旗手。麻三寸把判词撕成两半，一半擦了瓜汁：「下回升堂，带着王的印来。」

Once the halberdiers go down, the judge crawls out from under his bench and kneels to present his verdict to Three-Inch Ma with both hands. Then he buys two melons out of his own pocket, one for Ma and one pressed on your standard-bearer. Ma tears the verdict in half and wipes melon juice off with one half. 'Next time you hold court, bring the King's seal.'

name: 鞭哨坡
Whip-Crack Slope
before: 葛小轮一个人跑了，说要去找那辆水车。你们追到一道坡上，看见他被一伙国舅府的骑手围在中间，骑手们拿马鞭抽着沙子逗他。他手里也攥着一根鞭子，旧得发黑，甩起来啪的一声，比骑手们的都响。

Ge Xiaolun has run off alone, saying he'll find that water cart himself. You track him to a slope and find him ringed by the Royal Uncle's riders, lashing the sand with their whips to bait him. He grips a whip too, old and blackened, and when he cracks it, it rings louder than any of theirs.
after: 骑手们被打跑，葛小轮红着眼把鞭子给你们看，鞭杆上烙着一个「千」字，是他前天在马市上从一个货郎手里买的，花光了身上的钱。货郎说鞭子是在湖边林子里捡的，「挂在一棵树上，像是有人特意挂的」。

The riders driven off, Ge Xiaolun, red-eyed, shows you the whip: the character 'Qian' is branded on its stock. He bought it two days ago at the horse market from a pedlar, spending every coin he had. The pedlar said he found it in the woods by the lake, 'hung on a tree, like someone put it there on purpose'.

name: 禁苑林
The Forbidden Park
before: 湖边林子深处圈着一道高篱笆，里头是国舅府的禁苑，养着鹿和孔雀。篱笆门口守着府里最精的一支人马：铁骑在外，弓手上树，戟士守门。麻三寸打听到，那个画押「府中刘」的刘管事，案子一翻，就躲进了这里，整天跟孔雀待在一块儿，说孔雀不会作证。

Deep in the lakeside woods a high fence encloses the Royal Uncle's private park, stocked with deer and peacocks. At its gate stands the house's finest company: cavalry outside, archers in the trees, halberdiers at the gate. Three-Inch Ma has learned that Steward Liu, who signed 'Liu of the House', has hidden here ever since the case started to turn. He spends all day with the peacocks; peacocks, he says, can't testify.
after: 精兵散了，刘管事被你们从孔雀笼后头揪了出来，一身羽毛。他全招了：碗是国舅让他塞的，因为那小子到处打听那辆水车，「国舅说，千里号的事，一个字都不许再提」。可水车的事他不知道，「那是老王时候的事，问铁教头，那年他在宫里当差」。

The picked troops scatter, and you haul Steward Liu out from behind the peacock cages, covered in feathers. He confesses everything: the Royal Uncle had him plant the bowl, because the boy kept asking about that water cart. 'The Royal Uncle said not one more word about the Qianli caravan.' But the cart itself he knows nothing about. 'That was in the old King's time. Ask Drill Master Tie. He served in the palace that year.'

name: 童子操场
The Children's Drill Ground
before: 第二天你们回到场子，铁教头已经把三十个孩子排好了，个个骑着瘦马，手里换了真家伙。「你们要我的操典，」他说，「先跟他们练一场。他们练了三年，还没跟真人交过手。」孩子们挺着胸脯，最小的那个骑不上马，是被人抱上去的。

Next day you return to the ground, and Drill Master Tie has his thirty children drawn up, each on a scrawny horse, wooden staves swapped for real weapons. 'You want my manual,' he says. 'Spar with them first. They've drilled three years and never faced a real opponent.' The children puff out their chests. The smallest couldn't climb onto his horse and had to be lifted up.
after: 孩子们输了，可一个也没掉队。铁教头用独臂从怀里掏出一本油布包着的册子：王城禁军的操典，他教了三十年，一页页添，一页页改。「照着它操，一天顶别人好几天，」他说，「拿去营里用，兵会谢你们。」他又说：「葛家那孩子是我抓的。我拿着刘管事的话去宫里求，宫里回了一张纸：「查实再判」，字写得极工整。可纸还没出宫门，我就被国舅赶了出来。我替那孩子作证。」

The children lose, but not one breaks rank. With his one arm Drill Master Tie takes from his coat a book wrapped in oilcloth: the drill manual of the King's guard, which he taught for thirty years, adding a page here, correcting a page there. 'Drill by this and one day counts for several,' he says. 'Take it to your camp. The soldiers will thank you.' Then: 'I'm the one who arrested the Ge boy. I took Steward Liu's word to the palace and begged, and the palace sent back a slip of paper, ‘Verify before sentencing’, in a very neat hand. Before that paper even left the palace gate, the Royal Uncle had thrown me out. I'll testify for the boy.'

name: 拦证渡
The Witness Ferry
before: 要进城递状子，得先过这条河。渡口被一队国舅府的戟士拦着，渡船全拴在对岸，岸边贴着一张告示：「凡为葛案作证者，不得渡河。」捕雀老汉、守门翁、铁教头都跟在你们后头，捕雀老汉怀里还揣着一只黄雀，说要带着它进城，「它也看见了」。

To take the petition into the city you must first cross this river. The Royal Uncle's halberdiers hold the ferry, every boat tied up on the far bank, and a notice posted on the shore: 'No one testifying in the Ge case may cross.' The old bird catcher, the gatekeeper and Drill Master Tie are all following behind you. The bird catcher has a finch tucked in his coat and means to take it into the city. 'It saw too.'
after: 戟士们跳河跑了，渡船解了下来。守门翁上船前把旧灯笼点上了，说那年夜里水车出城，那个瘦先生提的就是这样一盏灯。船到河心，麻三寸清点人数：证人三个，证物两样，黄雀一只。「还差一样，」他说，「那辆车。」

The halberdiers jump in the river and flee, and the boats are untied. Before boarding, the gatekeeper lights his old lantern: the thin gentleman carried one just like it the night the water cart left the city. In midstream Three-Inch Ma takes stock: three witnesses, two exhibits, one finch. 'One thing still missing,' he says. 'That cart.'

name: 石车辙
Stone Wheel-Ruts
before: 一片干裂的泥板地，泥板上压着两道深深的车辙，泥干了，辙印硬得像刻在石头上。一伙国舅府的弓手在这里搭了个瞭望棚，把辙印当成了界线：越过辙的，射。葛小轮蹲下来量了量车轮的宽窄，手指头都在抖：「是王城的大水车，跟我爹赶的一样宽。」

A stretch of cracked mud flats with two deep wheel-ruts pressed into it; the mud dried and the ruts set hard as if carved in stone. Some of the Royal Uncle's archers have built a lookout shelter here and treat the ruts as a boundary: cross them and you're shot. Ge Xiaolun crouches to measure the wheel gauge, his fingers shaking. 'A big royal water cart. The same width as the one my father drove.'
after: 弓手们跑了，你们顺着辙走了一里。辙印越走越深，像车上装着很重的东西，一直往东，进了湖边的林子。辙边还有一行脚印，一个大脚，一个窄靴子，并排走的。葛小轮说：「大的是我爹。」

The archers flee and you follow the ruts for a li. They grow deeper as you go, as if the cart was heavily laden, running east into the lakeside woods. Beside them runs a line of footprints, one pair big, one pair narrow booted, walking side by side. 'The big ones are my father's,' says Ge Xiaolun.

name: 讼棍坡
Pettifoggers' Slope
before: 坡上搭着三顶讼棚，比麻三寸那顶阔气十倍，是国舅府养的讼棍，带着一帮打手。他们一见麻三寸，就当场递了三张状子告他：一告他偷瓜，二告他冒充讼师，三告他「舌头过长，有伤风化」。打手们把状子钉在了路中间的木桩上，不签收不许过。

Three law booths stand on the slope, ten times grander than Three-Inch Ma's, belonging to pettifoggers kept by the Royal Uncle's house and a gang of their bruisers. The moment they see Ma they serve him three suits on the spot: one for stealing melons, one for impersonating an advocate, and one for 'a tongue of excessive length, injurious to public morals'. The bruisers nail the suits to a post in the middle of the road: no passing until he signs for them.
after: 打手被打跑，讼棍们收起了状子。有个最老的讼棍拉住麻三寸，悄悄翻出一本老王时候的律书，指着一条给他看：「借物有契，虽未还，不为盗。」老讼棍叹口气：「我年轻时也想当个好讼师，后来饿怕了。这条你拿去用。」

The bruisers driven off, the pettifoggers pack up their suits. The oldest of them draws Three-Inch Ma aside and quietly turns up a law book from the old King's time, pointing to one article: 'Where a thing is borrowed under contract, though not yet returned, it is not theft.' He sighs. 'When I was young I wanted to be a good advocate too. Then I got scared of going hungry. Take this article and use it.'

name: 琉璃珠帐
The Glass-Bead Tent
before: 野地里一顶挂满琉璃珠帘的大帐，主人是个波斯珠宝商，鼻梁高，胡子卷，会说一口带腔的官话。他的帐子三个月没人敢进：国舅府要他把那只银碗认作宫里的东西，他不肯，府里就派了弓手守在帐外，谁来买珠子就往谁的脚边射一箭。他坐在帐里，一颗颗擦珠子，擦得比镜子还亮。

A great tent hung with glass-bead curtains out in the open country, its owner a Persian jeweller with a high nose and curled beard who speaks the court tongue with an accent. For three months no one has dared go in. The Royal Uncle's house wanted him to swear the silver bowl was palace property; he wouldn't, so the house posted archers outside to shoot at the feet of anyone who came to buy. He sits inside polishing his beads one by one until they shine brighter than mirrors.
after: 弓手们被赶走，珠宝商掀开珠帘请你们进去，珠子、宝石、银器随便换。麻三寸把当票给他看，他只瞄了一眼：「葡萄纹，是国舅府的私纹，宫里的碗刻的是石榴。」他又说：「我只认东西，不认人。东西不会撒谎，人会。」

The archers driven off, the jeweller parts his curtains and invites you in: beads, gems and silverware, trade what you like. Three-Inch Ma shows him the pawn ticket and he barely glances at it. 'Vine pattern. That's the Royal Uncle's private mark. Palace bowls are engraved with pomegranates.' Then: 'I vouch for things, not people. Things don't lie. People do.'

name: 夜袭棚
Night-Raid Camp
before: 麻三寸在野地里搭了个临时讼棚，证据都收在一只瓜筐里。半夜里一伙国舅府的戟士摸了过来，手里拎着火把，要烧筐。麻三寸被惊醒，抱着瓜筐满地乱跑，边跑边喊：「烧证据，罪加三等！」喊得比戟士的脚步声还响。

Three-Inch Ma has pitched a makeshift law booth in the open country, with all the evidence kept in a melon basket. At midnight some of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers creep up with torches to burn it. Woken, Ma runs about hugging the basket and yelling, 'Burning evidence raises the crime three degrees!', louder than the halberdiers' footsteps.
after: 戟士们被打跑，瓜筐保住了。从这天起，麻三寸睡觉把当票含在嘴里，判词压在枕下，律书垫在屁股底下。他清点了一遍：当票、证词、出城记、律条，「就差车」。葛小轮一夜没睡，在棚外甩鞭子，一声一声，像在叫谁。

The halberdiers driven off, the basket is saved. From that day Three-Inch Ma sleeps with the pawn ticket in his mouth, the verdict under his pillow and the law book under his backside. He takes stock: pawn ticket, testimony, gate log, the law. 'Just the cart missing.' Ge Xiaolun doesn't sleep at all. He stands outside cracking his whip, crack after crack, as if calling someone.

name: 登闻鼓
The Petition Drum
before: 王城外的大道边立着一面大鼓，叫登闻鼓，老王时候的规矩：有冤的人来敲，王必须听。鼓面被人用刀划成了一条条，鼓上站着两个国舅府的戟士，下面还有一队守着，谁来敲鼓，先打二十棍。麻三寸看着破鼓，把状纸攥得哗哗响。

Beside the high road outside the city stands a great drum, the Petition Drum. Under the old King's rule, anyone with a grievance could beat it and the King had to hear. Its skin has been slashed to ribbons; two of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers stand on top of it and a squad below, and anyone who comes to drum gets twenty strokes first. Three-Inch Ma looks at the ruined drum and his petition rustles in his fist.
after: 戟士们跑了，你们剥了一张驼皮给鼓重新蒙上。葛小轮抡起鼓槌敲了三下，鼓声传进城里。傍晚，城里跑出来一个小内侍，递来一张纸条，只有四个字：「带车来见。」字写得很工整，最后一笔像是收得太快，带出一道细尾巴。

The halberdiers flee and you stretch a camel hide over the drum. Ge Xiaolun swings the drumstick three times and the boom carries into the city. At dusk a young eunuch runs out with a slip of paper bearing four words: 'Bring the cart.' The hand is very neat, the last stroke lifted off a little too fast, trailing a fine tail.

name: 破车场
The Cart Breaker's Yard
before: 一片堆满破车的场子，车轮、车辕、车厢摞得像小山，是个收破烂的老汉的家当。可这几天场子被国舅府的弓手占了，他们把全城收来的旧车一辆辆浇油点火，烧得满天黑烟，说是「清理旧物」。老汉蹲在场边，烧一辆，他就掰一下指头。

A yard heaped with broken carts, wheels, shafts and bodies stacked like hills: the whole stock of an old scrap man. For days now the Royal Uncle's archers have occupied it, dousing the old carts collected from all over the city with oil and setting them alight one by one, the sky black with smoke, 'clearing out old rubbish'. The old man squats at the edge and bends down a finger for each cart burnt.
after: 弓手们跑了，火扑灭了，老汉的十个指头已经掰完了两轮。他说国舅这是在烧王城的水车，「烧了就没得找了」。可有一辆，他知道不在这里：「湖边林子里有一辆，十年了没人敢碰，说是闹鬼，夜里有人在车边点灯。」

The archers flee and the fires are beaten out; the old man has run through his ten fingers twice. The Royal Uncle is burning the city's water carts, he says, 'so there'll be none left to find'. But there's one he knows isn't here. 'There's one in the woods by the lake. Ten years nobody's dared touch it. They say it's haunted: at night someone lights a lamp beside it.'

name: 巡林骑
The Forest Patrol
before: 湖边林子里新开了一条马道，国舅府的骑手一天三趟来回巡，见人就盘问：「找车的？」答「是」的抓走，答「不是」的也抓走，说「不是的才可疑」。捕雀老汉说他认得进林子的小路，可小路口正好拴着几匹巡林的马。

A new bridle path has been cut through the lakeside woods, and the Royal Uncle's riders patrol it three times a day, questioning everyone: 'Looking for a cart?' Those who say yes are seized. Those who say no are seized too: 'The ones who say no are the suspicious ones.' The old bird catcher knows a footpath into the woods, but the patrol's horses happen to be tethered right at its mouth.
after: 巡林的骑手被打下马，跑了。捕雀老汉领着你们钻进小路，一路学鸟叫，林子里的鸟一路应着。他说鸟窝搭在哪里，哪里就有人很久没去过。走了半里，他指着树上一只旧鸟窝：窝底垫着的，是一截褪了色的车帘。

The patrol is knocked from the saddle and flees. The bird catcher leads you down the footpath, whistling birdcalls all the way, the birds of the wood answering. Where birds build, he says, no one has been for a long time. Half a li in, he points to an old nest in a tree: it's lined with a strip of faded cart curtain.

name: 车匠囚屋
The Wheelwright's Prison
before: 野地里一间上了锁的木屋，屋外守着一队国舅府的戟士，屋里关着王城的老车匠。他给老王造了一辈子车，每辆车的辕木上都刻着他自己的记号。国舅府怕他认出什么，把他关在这里，叫他天天削马桩子。老车匠隔着窗户喊：「我认得每一辆！」

A locked log cabin in the open country, guarded by the Royal Uncle's halberdiers, holds the King's city's old wheelwright. He built carts for the old King all his life and carved his own mark on the shaft of every one. Afraid of what he might recognise, the Royal Uncle's house has locked him up here to whittle hitching posts all day. The old wheelwright shouts through the window: 'I know every one of them!'
after: 戟士们跑了，门锁砸开。老车匠揉着手腕说，老王的水车一共造过十二辆，十一辆都烧了，他亲眼看着烧的。剩下那一辆，是老王亲手指给千里号的：「老王说，城里人能渴一天，外头那三百个人一天都渴不起。」他扛起刨子：「我跟你们去认车。」

The halberdiers flee and the lock is smashed. Rubbing his wrists, the old wheelwright says he built twelve water carts for the old King. Eleven have been burnt; he watched them burn. The last one the old King gave to the Qianli caravan with his own hand. 'The old King said: the city can go thirsty a day, but those three hundred outside can't go thirsty one day.' He shoulders his plane. 'I'll come and identify the cart.'

name: 纵火营
The Firebrand Camp
before: 林子边上扎着一座大营，戟士、弓手、铁骑三路排开，营里堆着成垛的干柴和十几桶火油。国舅府的最后一道令传到了：林子里那辆车，「连林子一块儿烧」。营头正带人往林边泼油，风往湖那边吹，一点火，半片林子都保不住。

A large camp sits at the edge of the woods, halberdiers, archers and cavalry in three ranks, stacks of dry firewood and a dozen barrels of lamp oil inside. The Royal Uncle's house has sent its last order: that cart in the woods is to be burnt 'along with the woods'. The camp captain is splashing oil along the tree line, and the wind blows towards the lake. One spark and half the forest is lost.
after: 大营被冲散，火把扔进了湖里，油桶滚进了泥塘。营头被绑起来的时候还在嘟囔：「一辆破车，至于吗？」老车匠拿刨子柄敲了他一下：「那不是破车，那是一城人借出去的一天的水。」

The camp is broken up, the torches thrown in the lake, the oil barrels rolled into a mud pond. As he's tied up the captain is still muttering: 'All this for one broken cart?' The old wheelwright raps him with the handle of his plane. 'That's no broken cart. That's a day's water a whole city lent.'

name: 借水车
The Borrowed Cart
before: 林子最深处，一片空地上停着一辆大水车，车轮陷进了土里一半，车辕上长了青苔，车边一根木杆，杆头挂着一盏灯，灯碗里的油是新添的。车周围埋伏着最后一伙国舅府的弓手，等着放火的人来。葛小轮看见车，鞭子都掉在了地上。

In the deepest part of the woods, in a clearing, stands a great water cart, its wheels half sunk in earth, moss on its shafts, a pole beside it with a lamp hanging at the top, the oil in the lamp freshly topped up. The last band of the Royal Uncle's archers lies in ambush around it, waiting for the fire-setters. At the sight of the cart, Ge Xiaolun drops his whip.
after: 弓手们跑了。老车匠摸到辕木上自己的记号。车厢里贴着一张纸：「借王城水车一辆，载水三十囊，予千里号三百人。账房记。来年以渠抵之。」麻三寸收好：「有契，不为盗。」葛小轮取下那盏灯抱在怀里：每夜是谁来添的油？他要把车拉进城，当着王的面对账。

The archers flee. The old wheelwright finds his own mark on the shaft and nods. Pasted inside the cart is a sheet of paper: 'Borrowed: one royal water cart, carrying thirty skins of water, for the three hundred of the Qianli caravan. Entered by the bookkeeper. To be repaid next year with a channel.' Three-Inch Ma peels it off and puts it away. 'A contract. No theft.' Ge Xiaolun takes down the lamp and holds it to his chest: who has been coming every night to fill it? He'll haul the cart into the city and settle this account in front of the King.

name: 截酒岗
Wine Ambush Ridge
before: 北边野地里，一支驼队被人截在岗下，几十峰骆驼驮着一摞摞酒坛子。截路的是国舅府的家丁和雇来的刀手，戟士、弓手、骑手都有，嚷嚷着「酒留下，人滚」。驼队的女头领手里只有一把长柄酒勺，站在坛子堆上，一勺一个，把爬上来的人敲下去。

In the northern open country a camel train has been cut off at the foot of a ridge, dozens of camels loaded with stacks of wine jars. The ambushers are the Royal Uncle's household men and hired blades, halberdiers, archers and riders, yelling 'Leave the wine and get lost!' The caravan's leader, a woman, has nothing but a long-handled wine ladle. She stands on the pile of jars knocking down each man who climbs up, one ladle a man.
after: 截路的人跑了，女头领从坛子堆上跳下来，自称柳三娘，北边葡萄园的酒驼子。她说这是给王城送的春酒：每年开春，宫里都订二百九十九坛，一坛不多，一坛不少，「我爹送了六年，从没错过一坛」。今年是她头一回送，国舅府却放话：春酒一坛都不许进城。

The ambushers flee and the woman jumps down from the jars. She's Liu Sanniang, wine carrier for the northern vineyards. This is the spring wine for the King's city: every spring the palace orders two hundred and ninety-nine jars, not one more, not one less. 'My father delivered for six years and never missed a jar.' This is her first year, and the Royal Uncle's house has given out that not one jar of spring wine is to enter the city.

name: 尝酒卡
The Tasting Post
before: 路口一道木卡，卡上挂着「验酒」的牌子，守卡的是一队王城戟士，说是奉命查春酒里有没有毒。查法是：一坛一坛地喝。驼队到的时候，他们已经验了三坛，个个脸红脖子粗，抱着坛子喊三娘「再来一坛，这坛没验准」。

A wooden barrier at a crossroads hung with a sign, 'Wine Inspection', manned by a squad of royal halberdiers who say they're ordered to check the spring wine for poison. Their method: drink it, jar by jar. By the time the caravan arrives they've inspected three, every face flushed and neck swollen, and they're hugging the jars shouting at Sanniang for 'another one, this one wasn't checked properly'.
after: 戟士们醉倒在卡下，鼾声震天。柳三娘看着三只空坛子直跺脚：少了三坛，就不是二百九十九了。「宫里收酒的人每年都数三遍，」她说，「少一坛都不收。」她咬咬牙，决定绕路去北边的老窖里补上，「宁可多走三天，也不能缺数」。

The halberdiers collapse beneath their barrier, snoring like thunder. Liu Sanniang stamps her foot at the three empty jars: three short, and it isn't two hundred and ninety-nine any more. 'The palace men count three times every year,' she says. 'One jar short and they won't take any.' She grits her teeth and decides to detour to the old cellar in the north to make them up. 'Better three extra days than a short count.'

name: 漏酒林
The Leaking Wood
before: 驼队走进湖北边的林子，林子里忽然飞出一阵箭，不射人，专射坛子，一箭一个洞，酒顺着驼背往下淌，香得林子里的松鼠都探出了头。放箭的是黄家酒坊雇的弓手：黄家是国舅府的亲戚，眼红柳家的王单，「坛子漏了，明年的单子就是我们的」。

As the caravan enters the woods north of the lake, a flight of arrows suddenly comes out of the trees. They don't hit people. They hit jars, a hole an arrow, wine streaming down the camels' flanks, so fragrant the squirrels poke their heads out. The archers are hired by the Huang winery, kin of the Royal Uncle's house, jealous of the Liu family's royal order. 'Leaky jars, and next year's order is ours.'
after: 弓手们跑了，驼队里那个不说话的大个子箍桶匠拿手指头一个个堵住坛子上的洞，再糊上泥。柳三娘说她爹当年接这张单子，是宫里来了个瘦瘦的文书，一口酒没尝，就把钱数得清清楚楚，「多一文退一文，少一文补一文」。

The archers flee, and the caravan's silent giant of a cooper plugs the holes in the jars one by one with his fingers, then daubs them with clay. When her father took on this order, Liu Sanniang says, a thin clerk came from the palace, didn't taste a drop, and counted out the money to the last copper. 'One copper over and he'd return it; one under and he'd make it up.'

name: 高跷贼
The Stilt Thieves
before: 夜里驼队宿在野地，帐篷外忽然冒出一排人影，比骆驼还高，原来是一伙踩高跷的杂耍艺人，顶着空坛子来换满坛子，换完一个踩着高跷就跑。他们的弓手也站在高跷上放箭，晃晃悠悠，一箭都射不准，可也让人够不着。

The caravan camps in the open, and at night a row of figures taller than the camels rises outside the tents: a troupe of stilt-walking acrobats, swapping empty jars for full ones balanced on their heads and stilting off with each swap. Their archers shoot from stilts too, swaying so much not one arrow finds its mark, but no one can reach them either.
after: 大个子箍桶匠一抱一个，把高跷艺人连人带跷放倒了。他们是黄家雇来的，一人一天二十文，饿得慌。柳三娘听完，反手雇了他们：「顶坛子走路比骆驼稳，一人一天三十文，管饭。」第二天，驼队里多了一排踩高跷的，坛子顶在头上，一滴没洒。

The giant cooper hugs the acrobats down one at a time, stilts and all. The Huang family hired them at twenty coppers a day, and they were starving. Liu Sanniang hears them out and hires them on the spot. 'You carry jars steadier than camels. Thirty coppers a day and meals.' Next morning the caravan has a row of stilt-walkers with jars balanced on their heads, not a drop spilt.

name: 林官小屋
The Forest Warden's Lodge
before: 湖北的林子归一个老林官管，每年春酒过林子，都要在他的小屋前歇一夜。今年小屋被国舅府的一队戟士占了，林官被绑在门口的树上，戟士们把他的林册撕了生火，说这片林子「从今往后归黄家」。老林官看见驼队，第一句话是：「数够了吗？」

The woods north of the lake are kept by an old forest warden, and every spring the wine caravan spends a night outside his lodge on its way through. This year a squad of the Royal Uncle's halberdiers has taken the lodge and tied the warden to a tree at the door, tearing up his forest register to light their fire and declaring that these woods 'belong to the Huang family from now on'. When the old warden sees the caravan, his first words are: 'Is the count right?'
after: 戟士们跑了，老林官揉着胳膊，帮三娘把坛子数了一遍，又数一遍。他说宫里收酒的人每年在林边等，数三遍，数完就走，从不多说一句。他只问过一回：「为什么是二百九十九？」收酒的人说：「王说的，王的单子上，从来只有这个数。」

The halberdiers flee, and the old warden, rubbing his arms, helps Sanniang count the jars once, then again. Every year, he says, the palace men wait at the edge of the wood, count three times, and leave without another word. He asked only once: 'Why two hundred and ninety-nine?' The palace man said: 'The King's word. That's the only number his order has ever had.'

name: 回营骑
The Recall Riders
before: 林中空地上，一队王城铁骑截住了驼队，不要酒，要人：他们要带走那个不说话的大个子箍桶匠，说他是禁军逃兵，十年前在宫里当过差。大个子把坛子一个个放下，挡在三娘前头，攥紧了拳头。他不说话，可谁都看得出来，他不打算跟他们走。

In a woodland clearing a troop of royal cavalry blocks the caravan. They don't want wine; they want a man: the silent giant cooper, who they say is a deserter from the King's guard and served in the palace ten years ago. The giant sets down his jars one by one, steps in front of Sanniang and clenches his fists. He says nothing, but anyone can see he has no intention of going with them.
after: 铁骑们被打跑了。夜里大个子拿刀在一块木板上刻字给你们看：他以前守过宫里的酒窖。每年春酒入窖那一夜，王会一个人下来，不带灯，摸着坛子一个个数，数完坐在坛子中间，很久不走。「我看不见王的脸，」他刻道，「只听见他在数。」

The cavalry driven off, that night the giant carves words on a board with his knife to show you. He used to guard the palace wine cellar. Every spring, the night the wine went in, the King would come down alone, with no lamp, and count the jars by touch, one by one; then sit among them for a long time. 'I never saw the King's face,' he carves. 'I only heard him counting.'

name: 无园坡
Vineless Slope
before: 野地里一伙马贼拦住驼队，不抢酒，抢骆驼。领头的说他们原本是北边葡萄园里摘葡萄的，园子被黄家一片片买走，葡萄藤砍了改种棉花，摘葡萄的没了活路，只好骑上马抢东西。他们的马都瘦，马鞍是拿葡萄架子的木头钉的。

In the open a band of horse thieves stops the caravan. Not for the wine; for the camels. Their leader says they used to pick grapes in the northern vineyards, but the Huang family bought the vineyards up one by one, cut down the vines and planted cotton. With no picking work left they took to horses and robbery. Their mounts are thin, their saddles nailed together from old trellis wood.
after: 马贼们被打散，柳三娘却把领头的叫了回来：她的老窖还要人补酒、搬坛，「会摘葡萄的手，搬坛子不会摔」。领头的愣了半天，红了眼。他说当年千里号的人也在北边园子里帮过一季工，「三百个人，摘了一秋的葡萄，换了三百坛酒，说是存着，回来那天喝」。

The horse thieves are scattered, but Liu Sanniang calls the leader back: her old cellar needs hands to make up the wine and move jars. 'Hands that can pick grapes won't drop a jar.' The leader stares a long while, eyes reddening. Back then, he says, the Qianli people worked a season in the northern vineyards too. 'Three hundred men picked a whole autumn of grapes for three hundred jars of wine. They said they'd store it and drink it the day they came back.'
